# R397 — layer-major KV/state/capacity admission audit

Date: 2026-10-13 Asia/Tokyo. Read-only source and report review for restoring the historical `f263d87d44aa671d056c33e6c6b6b0635fc25b8c` SYCL layer-major prefill to the XeStrata root engine. Current source is frozen parent `8b48d17c99b70d32781f9f5b056602a598a37b1c` in `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-restore-layer-major-prefill-20261013`, read with `git show`; working-tree status was observed before inspection and no parent files were read from its dirty checkout. R394v2/R395v2 and the designated registry v193 were consulted. No source edits, build, test, GPU, model, service, cleanup, git mutation, secret inspection, or private-environment search was performed. This report is the only new write.

## Decision

Do not remove the old all-KV-resident guard to admit the current stock `context=262144, INT8 resident=32768` session. The historical layer-major implementation is an all-resident-KV algorithm. It accesses each QSA's layer-owned resident pool/page mapping and assumes the full prompt's cells are available there. Current streamed KV has a bounded resident cache plus host-authoritative backing and a separate full-context identity stage used by ordinary chunk-major prefill. Reusing only that ordinary stage or deleting the guard does not provide correct layer-major state lifecycle, and a 32,768-cell pool cannot represent arbitrary 262,144-cell sparse selections without an explicit streaming design.

The viable staged direction is (1) restore a narrowly admitted resident-only source prototype under a new opt-in for source/geometry diagnosis; (2) separately design a streamed-KV layer-major mode with explicit per-QSA stage ownership and state/capacity logic; and (3) do not call either complete 256K support until every QSA prefix, indexer, resident map, GDN/PLE state, save/restore, final cell, and following generation path is qualified. R3 and R5 already document a possible single active-QSA staging plane design and its required tests; it remains a proposal, not evidence of completion.

## Evidence and current route

R395v2 establishes that the historic route was developed under nested `sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`; current frozen parent uses root `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`. The old `Prefill::run_layer_major` explicitly admits only `kv_mode == 0` (all pages resident), compact FP16 fallback, full single-GPU layer range, stable expert source, and no PLE preload. It opens an expert cache sized for all experts in one layer, reads one layer's expert blobs once, and runs all prompt chunks for that layer before moving on. It preserves its resident KV path; it does not implement a streamed-KV layer-major schedule.

Current root prefill has no `run_layer_major` entry or historical layer-major selector. It has ordinary chunk-major `run` and supports QSA `kv_mode==1` streamed INT8 KV. Current `take_stage` allocates a full-context staging pool for ordinary per-chunk QSA execution (unless the A/B `STRATA_KV_STAGE_OWN` option owns it separately); the existing `kv_stage_from_host` prefix copy is performed for each chunk before attention. `kv_append` updates host authority, resident slots, and the identity stage. That stage is not equivalent to preserving an owner across all chunks for one QSA layer. Current root has no old `run_layer_major` guard to simply delete; a root restoration must define new admissions and lifecycle in current Runtime/ExpertSource/ExpertCache/workspace abstractions.

A stable expert source and one-layer-at-a-time expert cache are necessary for the transfer-reuse mechanism. They do not solve streamed QSA KV, and they do not establish fit. Current variable per-layer expert blob sizes mean the temporary cache must be sized for the maximum full layer range actually loaded, while every `(layer,expert)` residency mapping must match the current source and cache ownership. Cache/lease restoration, event completion before retiring the layer cache, and cancellation/error paths must be explicit.

## KV and persistent-state geometry

For the target geometry reported by R3 and confirmed by the QSA layout (`n_head_kv=2`, `head_dim=256`, page size 4), INT8 KV is 1,056 bytes per cell: K and V codes use 1,024 bytes and their group scales use 32 bytes. At 262,144 cells:

- One full host-authoritative QSA KV backing is 276,824,064 bytes (264 MiB). Twelve QSA layers require 3,321,888,768 bytes (3.09375 GiB), before metadata/alignment.
- A 32,768-cell resident cache is 34,603,008 bytes (33 MiB) per QSA, 396 MiB across 12 QSA layers, plus roughly 3 MiB of total page maps. It cannot be treated as a full-context pool.
- The ordinary full-context INT8 staging plane is 264 MiB for one active QSA; allocate one and reuse it, not twelve. This current chunk path refills/copies its prefix by chunk; a layer-major persistent owner would need explicit generation, QSA ordinal, `valid_cells`, and queue completion state.
- Twelve QSA indexer pooled arrays remain session state: approximately 32 MiB per layer / 384 MiB total, plus dead/tail/block-position state. One QSA owns shared RoPE tables of about 64 MiB. These states cannot be freed when the scheduler advances layers.
- The 36 GDN layers' recurrent state is approximately 3 MiB each / 108 MiB total before convolution history. PLE normalized history, convolution history, token window and `ple_prev` also remain persistent session state.

These figures represent different concurrent allocations. Host K/V is canonical state; the stage is scratch; the resident map is not the identity stage map. A bounded resident cache must resolve all selected cells or return a checked failure—never omit a selected page. `kv_stream_resolve`'s demand union can exceed resident capacity, so it is not a safe substitute for a full-prefix identity stage without proof for the actual selection pattern.

## Residual and allocator limits

The layer-major residual bridge is one FP32 plane with `D=10240` floats per token: 40,960 bytes/token. At 262,144 rows it is 10,737,418,240 bytes (10 GiB), impossible on a 10-GiB B570 alongside model weights, resident KV, caches, graph/runtime and workspaces. The old 32,768-row GPU prefix is 1.25 GiB. With a 32,768-row GPU prefix and full 262,144-token prompt, the host residual tail has 229,376 rows = 9.375 GiB. If GPU prefix is zero, host residual is the full 10 GiB. A “240K host tail” is therefore approximately 9.375 GiB, before the remaining host allocations.

GPU residual prefix selection must use fresh free VRAM after model weights, current expert/decode cache, current session KV and state, PLE/head allocations, graph/runtime reserve and every already-owned workspace. Then reserve the proposed one-layer expert cache, prompt workspace/scratch, head buffers, decode cache, persistent session allocations and callback-owned allocations, plus an explicit driver/runtime reserve. Total card capacity or a nominal VRAM fraction is not admission. Current `Prefill::bytes_needed`/workspace layout reports prompt workspace, not all simultaneously live engine/session memory; it cannot certify the complete peak alone. If an exact aggregate cannot be measured/reconciled, safely choose no GPU residual prefix or reject before mutating session state. Round the prefix down to a whole 8,192-token chunk after applying the first-chunk rule; do not round up. Check all products, sums, `vector::max_size`, allocation results and subtraction-based bounds before allocation/state mutation.

Host admission also needs an aggregate budget: 3.09375 GiB host KV plus up to 10 GiB residual bridge, plus PLE gather buffers (R3 records 160 MiB for two 8K×2560 FP32 buffers), other host arenas, expert-source data/stager pinned buffers, session/snapshot state, API/runtime overhead and OS headroom. Pageable fallback changes DMA behavior and does not reduce the logical bytes. The currently inspected records do not establish an exact target-machine free-host-memory budget for a 256K run; do not claim host fit from arithmetic alone.

## State, boundaries and generation

Each QSA's host KV, resident slots/map, indexer pooled rows and tail/dead state persist independently. GDN recurrence/convolution and PLE history advance in model-layer order; `ple_prev` and token history must preserve their existing cross-layer semantics. Final capture/checkpoint must see the standard complete session state. A shared stage can be reassigned only after all readers and copies of its prior QSA owner complete. For resumed `pos0>0`, seed exactly `[0,pos0)` from that QSA's host backing, including partial pages; for `pos0=0`, skip empty seed. Append current cells into host canonical storage and the owned stage before attention; advance valid extent only after ordered append completion. Keep identity stage mapping distinct from resident page mapping and disable/coordinate ordinary next-QSA prefetch while stage ownership is retained.

The configured valid positions are 0..262143; a count of 262144 is full capacity. The final one-cell tail at position 262143 must work. Test both full prefill ending with append at 262143 and a 262143-cell prefix followed by generation at 262143. A subsequent append at position 262144 must reject. Also test 4095/4096 page boundaries, chunk boundaries, partial-page tails 1/2/3, last cell in a full page, resumed prefix, SAVE/RESTORE at counts 262143 and 262144, and a subsequent GEN token where capacity permits. Check exact host KV codes/scales, resident page maps/slots after resolution, indexer dead/tail/pooled/block state, every GDN recurrence/conv state, PLE history/`ple_prev`, logits and selected IDs against unchanged chunk-major execution.

## Stable expert/cache constraints and qualification order

A resident-only diagnostic prototype should require: one device and full layer range; stable non-transient source whose blobs remain valid until copy completion; no helper/next/split/handoff/phase-cache interaction; no PLE preload; fixed 8K chunk; explicitly fixed FP16 fallback/MMQ policy matching PR #6; one-layer cache sized for the largest loaded layer; exact full-resident QSA geometry; and fresh aggregate VRAM admission. Residency may be published only after copy completion. Cancellation/failure must drain compute, copy and source/stager readers before cache retirement and restore cache/session callbacks. This narrow prototype is not the current 256K streamed stock configuration.

For stream support, first prove the single-active-QSA stage owner path at short context, including multiple chunks and resumed partial page; then 32K and just over the 32K resident extent to exercise cache eviction/demand resolution; then full 256K all-layer execution, full state comparison, SAVE/RESTORE, last-cell and following GEN checks, queue/failure/cancel behavior, and measured host/VRAM peak. Only after these checks may performance be measured. Resident-only prototype results cannot be generalized to stream support.

## Safe old-vs-current comparison

R394v2 records a valid historic PR #6 32K win: three alternating pairs, same binary/fixture, all logits/output match, 453.2935 tok/s baseline vs 645.848 tok/s layer-major median, 29.814% lower wall time for that recipe. It used 65,538 context with all K/V resident, 8K chunks, cache 128, `compact=2`, `layer_major=1`, a 32K FP32 GPU residual prefix, MMQ-off FP16 fallback, one greedy output token, no phase/transfer markers or PLE preload. Preserve this as historic recipe-specific evidence.

It is not a matched performance comparison to the current stock 262144-context, INT8-resident-32768 run: prompt length, generation length, K/V policy/context, cache, binary/compiler/source/client, timer path and default MMQ selection differ. Do not extrapolate or report a 646-to-current tok/s regression. First reproduce the historical recipe on current source with identical fixture, token count, context/KV policy, chunk, cache, MMQ-off policy, one-token horizon, timer and output checks; then compare current chunk-major and reviewed opt-in resident-only layer-major in interleaved fresh processes. Keep an MMQ-on campaign separate. Test full 256K correctness/capacity before interpreting speed, and compare a streamed mode only with its matched streamed chunk-major control. Do not route a 256K request through resident-only layer-major by silently changing only main-model KV while auxiliary/MTP state streams.
